summary.en: Elders are being urged to use their influence to prevent conflict while a Sudanese official accuses Ethiopia and South Sudan of fuelling regional instability, and the election delay deepens the democratic crisis. A Christian woman was killed by her brother for trying to escape a forced marriage to a Muslim man, a boda-boda rider was shot dead by an armed passenger in Wau, and two Kapoeta youth were killed after an SSPDF arrest. Joint security talks between South Sudan and Sudan resumed in Juba, China urged the UN to lift sanctions, and the US set expectations for locally funded elections. Two battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Eldre blir oppfordret til å bruke sin innflytelse for å hindre konflikt, mens en sudansk tjenestemann anklager Etiopia og Sør-Sudan for å bidra til regional ustabilitet, og valgforsinkelsen forverrer den demokratiske krisen. En kristen kvinne ble drept av sin bror fordi hun prøvde å flykte fra et tvangs- ekteskap med en muslimsk mann, en boda-boda-sjåfør ble skutt og drept av en bevæpnet passasjer i Wau, og to unge fra Kapoeta ble drept etter et arrestasjon av SSPDF. Felles sikkerhetssamtaler mellom Sør-Sudan og Sudan ble gjenopptatt i Juba, Kina oppfordret FN til å oppheve sanksjonene, og USA satte forventninger til lokalt finansierte valg. To dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
